text:
Joel Farabee is having the best scoring start of his career in Calgary. He has 18 points in 22 games, nine on the power play, and is getting 19:11 a night, up to 19:35 over the last ten. Last season he managed 38 points in 82 games.

The jump is mostly real. His own chances are up a lot: 1.08 expected goals per 60, against 0.71 last season, and seven goals on 7.6 expected says his finishing is honest. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him as a rush player, 61% of his shots off transition, and Evolving-Hockey liked one quieter part of his game: he drew enough more penalties than he took to be worth about two goals from that alone.

Our range thinks his scoring pace will drift back some, toward 1.9 points per 60 from 2.6, because his point rate is ahead of his chances and the Flames' five-on-five play with him is about even. The last ten are already closer to normal, seven points against eight we'd expect. Still, a 26-year-old finding a top-six role on a new team is a good story.
